title: Suncom Joy Sensor
subtitle: A joystick with no stick — a printed eight-direction ring you stroke with your thumb on a touch panel
blurb: Suncom's 1983 Atari 2600 controller was described by its maker as a "touch-sensitive joystick simulator": a 6.5 x 3 inch slab, shaped like a TV remote, whose underside carries a 1.75-inch circular touch pad with the eight joystick directions printed on it. Hold it in one hand, stroke the pad with the other thumb, and the lightest touch moves the game; a slide switch mechanically locks out diagonals, and a second touch surface on the top face carries two fire pads, a rapid-fire sensor, and — uniquely — a second thumb-controllable fire pad. No lever, no dome, no travel.
